front_matter.preface: The Naga Tribes of Manipur (Tangkhul Sections) by T. C. Hodson, late Assistant Political Agent in Manipur and Superintendent of the State (Macmillan and Co., Limited, London, 1911). Presents the authoritative historical and ethnographic documentation of the Tangkhul Nagas, their habitat, social organization, village headmanship, folktales, ballads, and linguistic survey.

chapters.title: Habitat, Geography & Tribal Divisions
chapters.summary: Geographical territory and four subdivisions: Raphei, Kathur, Kamo, and Kharao.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Tangkhul miyur hi Manipur wui kaphung zanshorli pamda kaphung khangacheo eina ngashitna. Ayur khani eina mati leiyi: Raphei (Northern Tangkhuls), Kathur (Central Tangkhuls around Ukhrul), Kamo (Southern Tangkhuls bordering Maring territory), and Kharao (Western Tangkhuls facing the valley). Ukhrul kaphung hi phungreitang sada kaphung khangateiwui tui ngazekpam thada leiyi.
chapters.english_translation: The Tangkhuls occupy the mountain tracts east of the valley of Manipur. They are grouped into four main territorial sections: Raphei in the north, Kathur in the centre around Ukhrul and Hungpung, Kamo in the south, and Kharao in the west. Ukhrul serves as the recognized linguistic standard among all regional dialects.
grammar_points: Locative case marker -li attached to geographical names.
comprehension_questions: What are the four historical subdivisions of the Tangkhul territory?
Why was Ukhrul selected as the central standard by early linguists?

chapters.title: Tangkhul Linguistic Classification & Dialects
chapters.summary: Agglutinative morphology, vowel length contrasts, and Tibeto-Burman affiliations.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Tangkhul language exhibits agglutinative morphology with dominant prefix ka- forming adjectives and infinitives. Case relationships are indicated by postpositional affixes: -na (agentive), -li (dative/locative), -wui (genitive). Vowel length contrasts: 'sa' (to do) vs 'sā' (animal/flesh); 'mik' (eye) vs 'mei' (fire).
chapters.english_translation: Linguistic features of Tangkhul: Extensive use of prefixes and suffixes. Nominal and adjectival derivation through prefix ka-. Case markers function as postpositional clitics. Phonemic vowel length distinguishes essential vocabulary pairs.
grammar_points: Agglutinative affix ordering in verbal complexes.
comprehension_questions: Give two examples of minimal vowel length pairs in Tangkhul.
Which prefix is predominantly used to form infinitives?

chapters.title: Village Organization & The Awunga (Headman)
chapters.summary: Hereditary chieftainship (Awunga), the village council (Hangva), and clan clans (Shangnao).
chapters.tangkhul_text: Khaung kachida Awunga akha leiyi; Awunga hi shimkhurwui mathun eina ngashitna. Hangva council eina ngasoda ram shiyan kashak saikora ngazekseri. Shangnao kachida paman kathana mi akhakhana hangvali zangda khaungwui ot ngazeka.
chapters.english_translation: Every Tangkhul village is an autonomous democratic unit under a hereditary chief called the Awunga. The Awunga rules in consultation with the village council (Hangva), comprised of representatives from each clan (Shangnao), managing village land, disputes, and seasonal festivals.
grammar_points: Honorific register associated with the Awunga.
comprehension_questions: What is the role of the Hangva in village governance?
How is the position of Awunga inherited?

chapters.title: Traditional Laws, Land Tenure & Feasts of Merit
chapters.summary: Maran (Feasts of Merit), Tarung monuments, and terraced land rights.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Maran kashak hi Tangkhul ngashanli khamataiya otsak akhana. Tarung thingrei vakhang eina shimli shona. Seichang kala hok kachung khami eina ramnaoli shongza kashak saikora ngashitna. Lungto kala lungchan shoda awo-ayiwui machut saikora chimiksho chitheiya.
chapters.english_translation: The Feasts of Merit (Maran) represent the summit of customary social achievement. The celebrant earns the right to erect the carved Tarung monument post before his house. Mithuns and cattle are slaughtered to feast the entire community, and megalithic stone platforms are built.
grammar_points: Instrumental clitic -eina in monument dragging chants.
Nominal compounds combining animal terms and festive rites.
comprehension_questions: What privileges does a celebrant gain by performing Maran?
Describe the physical appearance and cultural meaning of the Tarung.

chapters.title: Tangkhul Folktales: Origin of the Species & Animals
chapters.summary: Mythological origin legends and the ancient brotherhood of hill and valley.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Awo-ayiwui khararchanli: 'Avah Samsokli tungthuiya, Makungana ili phungtung.' Chinaoni khani: kakhara a kaphungli leiyi, kakhanao a ngaleili vaipama. Meitei eina Tangkhul chinaoni thada kum kachida Mera Hou Chongba phanitli leikashi chithei ngaroka.
chapters.english_translation: Tangkhul mythology traces common origins from Samsok in the eastern hills. Tradition holds that two brothers parted ways: the elder brother settled in the misty Tangkhul heights, while the younger brother cultivated the fertile valley, establishing a bond renewed at the annual Mera festival.
grammar_points: Comparative conjunction thada (like, in the manner of).
comprehension_questions: What does the Samsok migration legend signify?
How is the kinship between Meiteis and Tangkhuls celebrated traditionally?

chapters.title: Traditional Tangkhul Ballads & Folk Poetry
chapters.summary: The epic ballad of Shimreishang and Maitonphi, and heroic martial poetry.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Shimreishang eina Maitonphiwui leikashiyi Tangkhul thotchanli kaphapamei laana. 'Avayo avayo, makhamalu Maitonphili rasha saka; sakhangaiye Maitonphi kharam thuihaowa.' Kazeiramli anili ngazipda kumching kumching leikashi ngazipsera.
chapters.english_translation: The tragic romance of Shimreishang and Maitonphi is the most famous epic ballad of the Tangkhuls. Forced apart by parental opposition and village taboos, their spirits are finally united in Kazeiram, the tranquil land of the departed where true lovers dwell forever.
grammar_points: Antiphonal dialogue structure in romantic verse.
Poetic vocabulary substitutions in folk metrics.
comprehension_questions: Why is the story of Shimreishang and Maitonphi significant in Tangkhul literature?
What is Kazeiram in traditional Tangkhul eschatology?

excerpts.tangkhul_text: Khaung kachida Awunga akha leiyi; Awunga hi shimkhurwui mathun eina ngashitna. Hangva council eina ngasoda ram shiyan kashak saikora ngazekseri. Shangnao kachida paman kathana mi akhakhana hangvali zangda khaungwui ot ngazeka.
excerpts.translation_en: Every Tangkhul village is an autonomous democratic unit under a hereditary chief called the Awunga. The Awunga rules in consultation with the village council (Hangva), comprised of representatives from each clan (Shangnao), managing village land, disputes, and seasonal festivals.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 4: Traditional Laws, Land Tenure & Feasts of Merit
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Maran kashak hi Tangkhul ngashanli khamataiya otsak akhana. Tarung thingrei vakhang eina shimli shona. Seichang kala hok kachung khami eina ramnaoli shongza kashak saikora ngashitna. Lungto kala lungchan shoda awo-ayiwui machut saikora chimiksho chitheiya.
excerpts.translation_en: The Feasts of Merit (Maran) represent the summit of customary social achievement. The celebrant earns the right to erect the carved Tarung monument post before his house. Mithuns and cattle are slaughtered to feast the entire community, and megalithic stone platforms are built.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 5: Tangkhul Folktales: Origin of the Species & Animals
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Awo-ayiwui khararchanli: 'Avah Samsokli tungthuiya, Makungana ili phungtung.' Chinaoni khani: kakhara a kaphungli leiyi, kakhanao a ngaleili vaipama. Meitei eina Tangkhul chinaoni thada kum kachida Mera Hou Chongba phanitli leikashi chithei ngaroka.
excerpts.translation_en: Tangkhul mythology traces common origins from Samsok in the eastern hills. Tradition holds that two brothers parted ways: the elder brother settled in the misty Tangkhul heights, while the younger brother cultivated the fertile valley, establishing a bond renewed at the annual Mera festival.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 6: Traditional Tangkhul Ballads & Folk Poetry
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Shimreishang eina Maitonphiwui leikashiyi Tangkhul thotchanli kaphapamei laana. 'Avayo avayo, makhamalu Maitonphili rasha saka; sakhangaiye Maitonphi kharam thuihaowa.' Kazeiramli anili ngazipda kumching kumching leikashi ngazipsera.
excerpts.translation_en: The tragic romance of Shimreishang and Maitonphi is the most famous epic ballad of the Tangkhuls. Forced apart by parental opposition and village taboos, their spirits are finally united in Kazeiram, the tranquil land of the departed where true lovers dwell forever.
